item.title: Bodies in dialogue
item.description: Every ensemble creates its own gravity, pulling and pushing in an endless conversation of weight and balance.

item.title: Every restriction is an invitation
item.description: Limitations don’t confine creativity; they become the source of unexpected possibilities.

item.title: Imperfection is truth
item.description: The most honest performance embraces the beautiful accidents that emerge from human presence.

item.title: Meaning can't be created.
item.description: The only thing choreography can do, is the creation of conditions, which allow for the emergence of meanings.

item.title: Movement is a dialogue with time
item.description: Dance exists in the conversation between what was and what will be, never fully captured in the present moment.

item.title: Movement transcends language
item.description: When words fail, the body speaks truths that language cannot contain.

item.title: Nothing which is finished, is alive.
item.description: A choreographic work, as well as all of its components, must remain a permanent draft.

item.title: Repetition is transformation
item.description: Each time we repeat a movement, we discover it anew, making repetition not a loop but a spiral.

item.title: Silence is movement
item.description: The pause between gestures is as choreographed as the motion itself.

item.title: Space is our canvas
item.description: The body doesn’t move through space, it creates it with every gesture.

item.title: The audience completes the work
item.description: Performance exists in the space between dancer and witness, completed by the act of being seen.

item.title: The body remembers
item.description: Memory isn’t just mental - it lives in our muscles, bones, and the spaces between movements.

item.title: The present is infinite
item.description: Each performance exists only in the moment of its creation, making every instance both eternal and ephemeral.

item.title: Time is elastic
item.description: In dance, a moment can stretch into eternity or compress into a heartbeat.

item.title: Start Here
item.description: The Gat Method is a collection of choreographic tools and practices that have been developed through the last 20 years, in the studio, on stage and in life. It was started by Emanuel Gat and it continues through all of us. You can join or book one of our workshops.

item.title: About The Gat Method
item.description:
The Gat Method is an innovative approach to dance and movement developed by renowned choreographer Emanuel Gat. This method represents a unique perspective on choreographic creation and dance training, drawing from Gat’s extensive experience as a creator and his work with dancers worldwide.

Core Principles

The method is built upon several key principles that challenge traditional approaches to dance and choreography:

  • Emergent Choreography: Rather than predetermined sequences, the method emphasizes the creation of movement through real-time decision-making and response.
  • Collective Intelligence: Focusing on the dynamic relationships between dancers and their ability to create complex patterns through simple interactions.
  • Adaptive Systems: Understanding dance as a living, breathing system that evolves through the continuous interaction of its participants.

item.title: Workshops
item.description:
Our workshops are immersive experiences designed to help you experience the Gat Method. Each workshop usually consists of a minimum of 3 days, which are taught by one or more of us. During these intensive sessions, participants engage in practical exercises, group discussions, and receive personalized feedback to deepen their understanding and application of the method.
